summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of pseudotumor cerebri and recent VP shunt placement was admitted for persistent right lower quadrant abdominal pain and migraine headaches. Imaging confirmed the shunt was correctly positioned with no intracranial complications. Surgical and neurosurgical evaluations found no acute cause for her pain. She was managed with increased gabapentin to 400 mg every eight hours and initiated on a lidocaine patch for neuropathic pain, with reported mild improvement. Her headache was consistent with her usual migraines and responded to home medications. Chronic issues including hypertension, diabetes, depression, and anemia were monitored and managed. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged in pain clinic, primary care, and ophthalmology for diplopia.
